data.content_ref: inline:Split the fixed-point computation into two passes: Pass 1 computes the skeptical labeling under a restricted rule that disallows reinstatement (a node is accepted only if directly defended by an attacked attacker); Pass 2 promotes to the full extension only if the restricted labeling's accepted set equals the intersection of all complete extensions restricted to that subgraph, i.e., reinstatement is admitted only when it introduces no new conflict. This makes reinstatement a checked, gated step rather than a purely derived one, changing the accepted/rejected boundary for cyclic cases. Determinism is preserved because both passes are deterministic; the criticizable claim is that the Pass-2 gate is not polynomial in general, and that 'no new conflict' smuggles in a second semantic commitment that may not respect the school's unifier stance (SRC_001).
